_meta.description: Starter dataset of major Indian central government farmer schemes for the AI matching feature. Feed this whole file (or the relevant subset) into the LLM prompt as grounding context alongside the farmer's profile.
_meta.important: Figures (amounts, percentages, caps) are current as of this research pass but government schemes are revised in budgets and policy updates. Verify against myscheme.gov.in, pmkisan.gov.in, and the respective ministry site before final submission. Do not let the app state a figure with more confidence than this dataset warrants — treat 'last_verified' as a prompt to re-check, not a guarantee.

schemes.name: PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi)
schemes.purpose: Direct income support for landholding farmer families.

excludes: serving/retired government employees above certain grades
professionals (doctors, engineers, lawyers, CAs) in practice
eligibility.other_conditions: Must be a landholding farmer family as per land records.

schemes.benefit: ₹6,000 per year, paid in three installments of ₹2,000 directly to the farmer's bank account.
schemes.how_to_apply: Register on the PM-KISAN portal or through the local Common Service Centre (CSC) with land records and Aadhaar.
schemes.notes: Very high match rate — this should surface for almost any landholding farmer who isn't in the excluded categories.

schemes.name: PM Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY)
schemes.purpose: Voluntary contributory pension scheme for small and marginal farmers.

eligibility.other_conditions: Landholding must be up to 2 hectares. Entry age 18-40; pension begins at 60.

schemes.benefit: Minimum ₹3,000 monthly pension after age 60. Government matches the farmer's monthly contribution (contribution amount depends on entry age).
schemes.how_to_apply: Enroll via Common Service Centre with Aadhaar and bank passbook.
schemes.notes: Good match for younger small/marginal farmers thinking about long-term security.

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)
schemes.purpose: Crop insurance against yield loss from natural calamities, pests, and disease.

eligibility.crop_type: notified crops in notified areas (varies by state/season)
eligibility.other_conditions: Participation is voluntary (since Kharif 2020) for both loanee and non-loanee farmers.

schemes.benefit: Compensation for crop loss from drought, flood, pests, and disease. Farmer premium capped at 2% for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops, and up to 5% for commercial/horticultural crops — government subsidizes the rest.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply through banks (if loanee), CSCs, insurance company portals, or the PMFBY portal before the season's cutoff date.
schemes.notes: Match strongly if the farmer grows a notified crop; note that notified crop lists vary by state and season.

schemes.name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC)
schemes.purpose: Short-term, low-interest institutional credit for crop production and allied activities.

eligibility.other_conditions: Owner-cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees, and sharecroppers are all eligible.

schemes.benefit: Credit up to ₹3 lakh at an effective ~4% interest rate (2% interest subvention plus 3% prompt-repayment incentive) for seeds, fertilizer, and irrigation needs.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply at any nationalized bank, regional rural bank, or cooperative bank branch.
schemes.notes: Broadly applicable — almost every actively cultivating farmer is a plausible match.

schemes.name: PM Krishi Sinchayee Yojana — Per Drop More Crop (PMKSY-PDMC)
schemes.purpose: Subsidizes micro-irrigation (drip/sprinkler) systems to improve water-use efficiency.

eligibility.crop_type: any, especially water-intensive or horticultural crops
eligibility.other_conditions: Higher subsidy assistance for small and marginal farmers; relevant for farmers in water-scarce or rain-fed areas.

schemes.benefit: Combined central + state subsidy of roughly 45-55% on drip and sprinkler irrigation systems.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply through the state agriculture/horticulture department or empanelled irrigation equipment vendors.
schemes.notes: Strong match for farmers who report irrigation access as poor/rain-fed.

schemes.name: Soil Health Card Scheme
schemes.purpose: Provides farmers a personalized soil nutrient report with fertilizer recommendations.

eligibility.other_conditions: Open to all farmers seeking soil testing; cards are reissued roughly every 2-3 years.

schemes.benefit: Free soil test covering ~12 parameters with tailored fertilizer/nutrient recommendations to improve yield and reduce input cost.
schemes.how_to_apply: Contact the local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or agriculture department soil-testing lab.
schemes.notes: Universally applicable — safe to recommend to almost any farmer profile as a low-effort, free next step.

schemes.name: PM-KUSUM
schemes.purpose: Promotes solar-powered irrigation pumps and grid-connected solar for farmers.

eligibility.other_conditions: Relevant to farmers currently relying on diesel pumps or facing high electricity costs for irrigation.

schemes.benefit: Subsidy split typically ~30% central + 30% state + 40% farmer contribution for solar pump sets (more favorable split in NE/hilly states), reducing recurring power/diesel costs.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply through the state renewable energy development agency (e.g., via the PM-KUSUM state portal).
schemes.notes: Good match when a farmer mentions high irrigation running costs or diesel pump dependency.

schemes.name: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)
schemes.purpose: Promotes cluster-based organic farming with certification support.

eligibility.other_conditions: Farmer must join or help form a cluster; uses Participatory Guarantee System (PGS) certification, not third-party certification.

schemes.benefit: Financial assistance of up to roughly ₹50,000 per hectare over three years for organic inputs, certification, and marketing support.
schemes.how_to_apply: Join through the state agriculture department's organic farming cell or an existing PKVY cluster.
schemes.notes: Match when the farmer expresses interest in organic/chemical-free farming or premium produce markets.

schemes.name: PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME)
schemes.purpose: Helps informal micro food-processing units (including farmer-run ones) formalize and grow.

eligibility.crop_type: any, especially farmers doing value-addition (e.g., pickles, flour, dairy products)
eligibility.other_conditions: Individual applicants: existing informal processing unit with annual turnover below ₹3 crore.

schemes.benefit: 35% credit-linked capital subsidy, capped at ₹10 lakh per individual unit.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply via the state's PMFME nodal agency or district resource person.
schemes.notes: Match when the farmer processes/sells value-added produce rather than only raw crop.

schemes.name: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)
schemes.purpose: Financing for post-harvest management and community farming infrastructure (e.g., storage, cold chain, processing units).

eligibility.other_conditions: Best suited to farmers/groups planning shared infrastructure investment rather than individual small purchases.

schemes.benefit: 3% per annum interest subvention on loans up to ₹2 crore for up to seven years, plus credit guarantee support.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply through the AIF online portal or a participating bank/NBFC.
schemes.notes: More relevant to FPOs/groups than individual smallholders — flag this distinction in the match explanation.

schemes.name: Formation and Promotion of 10,000 FPOs
schemes.purpose: Supports farmers organizing into Farmer Producer Organizations for collective bargaining and market access.

special_groups: farmer groups (300+ members in plains, 100+ in NE/hilly areas)
eligibility.other_conditions: Requires organizing as a Producer Company or Cooperative, not an individual application.

schemes.benefit: Equity grant of up to ₹2,000 per member (capped at ₹15 lakh per FPO), credit guarantee up to ₹2 crore, plus management support for 5 years.
schemes.how_to_apply: Approach the state's FPO Implementing Agency (e.g., NABARD, SFAC) to join or help form an FPO.
schemes.notes: Match when a farmer mentions wanting better market prices, collective selling, or existing informal farmer groups.

schemes.name: Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM)
schemes.purpose: Improves access to farm machinery and equipment, especially for small and marginal farmers.

eligibility.other_conditions: Custom Hiring Centres/village machinery banks receive higher subsidy shares than individual purchases.

schemes.benefit: 40-50% subsidy for individual equipment ownership; up to 80% for village-level machinery banks/custom hiring centres.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply through the state agriculture mechanization department or the Direct Benefit Transfer in Agriculture Mechanization (DBT-Agri) portal.
schemes.notes: Match when a farmer mentions manual labor bottlenecks, high labor cost, or wanting tractors/tillers/harvesters.

schemes.name: Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM)
schemes.purpose: Supports conservation and genetic improvement of indigenous cattle and buffalo, aiding dairy farmers.

eligibility.other_conditions: Relevant to farmers who keep cattle/buffalo, including those with little or no cropland.

schemes.benefit: Subsidy on sex-sorted semen (up to ~₹750/dose) and IVF services (up to ~₹5,000/pregnancy) to improve herd productivity.
schemes.how_to_apply: Contact the local veterinary/animal husbandry department or dairy cooperative.
schemes.notes: Include when the farmer's profile mentions livestock/dairy alongside or instead of crops.

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)
schemes.purpose: Develops the fisheries sector, including inland and aquaculture farming.

eligibility.other_conditions: Relevant to farmers with ponds/tanks or interest in aquaculture diversification.

schemes.benefit: 40-60% subsidy on fisheries-related assets (ponds, hatcheries, cold chain) plus ₹5 lakh group accident insurance for registered fishers.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply through the state fisheries department.
schemes.notes: Only surface this when the farmer mentions fish farming/aquaculture or has water bodies on their land.

schemes.name: National Beekeeping & Honey Mission (NBHM)
schemes.purpose: Promotes beekeeping and honey production as a supplementary income source.

eligibility.other_conditions: Especially relevant to farmers near orchards or oilseed crops where bees also boost pollination and yield.

schemes.benefit: Support for bee colonies and equipment, honey processing/testing infrastructure, and certification/traceability support.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply through the National Bee Board or state horticulture department.
schemes.notes: A good 'extra income' suggestion to pair with a primary-crop scheme match rather than a standalone recommendation.

schemes.name: Namo Drone Didi
schemes.purpose: Provides agricultural drones (for spraying fertilizer/pesticide as a paid service) to rural women's Self-Help Groups.

special_groups: Women Self-Help Groups federated under DAY-NRLM
eligibility.other_conditions: Beneficiary is the SHG, not an individual farmer directly — but individual women farmers can access drone spraying services through their local SHG.

schemes.benefit: 80% central subsidy (capped at ₹8 lakh) per SHG for a drone package plus training; the SHG then offers paid spraying services to farmers in the area.
schemes.how_to_apply: Through a woman farmer's local Self-Help Group federated under DAY-NRLM.
schemes.notes: Present as 'a service you can access via your local women's SHG' rather than a direct individual benefit, to avoid overpromising.
